column15:
Pemerintah Kota Pontianak menempatkan isu iklim sebagai bagian penting dalam pengawasan pembangunan daerah. Hal ini dilakukan melalui pemantauan indikator kunci seperti penurunan emisi gas rumah kaca, indeks risiko bencana, serta indeks ketahanan daerah. Data yang dihimpun oleh Dinas Lingkungan Hidup (DLH) dan Badan Penanggulangan Bencana Daerah (BPBD) menjadi dasar untuk melihat sejauh mana kota mampu menekan dampak perubahan iklim, sekaligus mengukur kesiapan dalam menghadapi bencana yang kerap melanda wilayah dataran rendah seperti Pontianak.

Selain pemantauan, pengawasan juga diwujudkan melalui strategi adaptasi dan mitigasi. Pemerintah merancang penguatan infrastruktur, termasuk tengah menginisiasi sistem peringatan dini banjir, drainase, dan ruang terbuka hijau berkelanjutan. Program ini dipadukan dengan kebijakan pengurangan emisi melalui energi terbarukan dan rehabilitasi lahan kritis. Upaya tersebut tidak hanya berorientasi pada pencegahan, tetapi juga menciptakan tata ruang kota yang lebih tangguh, ramah lingkungan, serta mendukung keberlanjutan ekosistem.

Di sisi lain, pengawasan terhadap isu iklim juga melibatkan kolaborasi multisektoral. Pemerintah membuka ruang kerja sama dengan masyarakat, sektor swasta, serta akademisi dalam memperkuat kesadaran publik mengenai adaptasi iklim. Edukasi menjadi bagian penting agar setiap lapisan masyarakat dapat berperan aktif dalam pengelolaan lingkungan. Dengan kombinasi pemantauan indikator, kebijakan adaptif, dan keterlibatan publik, pengawasan isu iklim di Pontianak diarahkan bukan hanya sebagai tanggung jawab pemerintah, tetapi juga gerakan kolektif menuju kota yang lebih resilien.
column16:
Isu perubahan iklim telah memberi dampak nyata terhadap arah perencanaan pembangunan di Kota Pontianak sebagaimana tertuang dalam Ranwal RPJMD Kota Pontianak 2025-2029. Sebagai kota dataran rendah yang rentan terhadap banjir, abrasi, dan cuaca ekstrem, pembangunan tidak lagi dapat dilepaskan dari agenda mitigasi dan adaptasi iklim. Pemerintah menetapkan indikator kunci seperti emisi gas rumah kaca, indeks risiko bencana, dan indeks ketahanan daerah sebagai acuan dalam menyusun kebijakan. Dengan begitu, pembangunan yang dilakukan tidak hanya mengejar pertumbuhan ekonomi, tetapi juga memperkuat resiliensi kota terhadap ancaman lingkungan yang semakin kompleks.

Dampak isu iklim terlihat jelas dalam prioritas pembangunan. Pontianak menekankan pentingnya infrastruktur hijau dan sistem peringatan dini yang berbasis teknologi, penguatan drainase, waduk, serta tanggul, hingga pengembangan ruang terbuka hijau (RTH) sebagai paru-paru kota. Selain itu, pemerintah memasukkan agenda restorasi lahan gambut dan konservasi ekosistem dalam perencanaan jangka menengah, karena fungsi kawasan ini sangat vital dalam menyerap karbon dan menjaga kestabilan iklim.

Pada level kebijakan, pemerintah menekankan pentingnya mitigasi dan adaptasi jangka panjang. Tata ruang kota diarahkan agar tidak membuka permukiman baru di kawasan rawan banjir, rehabilitasi lahan kritis dilakukan melalui program penghijauan, dan kebijakan energi mulai diarahkan pada penggunaan energi terbarukan. Semua ini menjadi bukti bahwa isu iklim kini menjadi faktor penentu dalam merancang arah pembangunan Pontianak.

Sejalan dengan itu, visi Wali Kota menegaskan pembangunan Pontianak yang berwawasan lingkungan dan humanis. Visi ini bermakna bahwa setiap kebijakan dan program tidak hanya harus ramah terhadap lingkungan, tetapi juga berpihak pada manusia, terutama masyarakat yang paling rentan terhadap dampak perubahan iklim. Dengan perspektif humanis, pembangunan tidak hanya berbicara tentang infrastruktur, melainkan juga tentang kualitas hidup, kesehatan, dan keberlanjutan sosial masyarakat.

Dengan kombinasi indikator ilmiah, strategi kebijakan adaptif, dan visi kepemimpinan yang berwawasan lingkungan serta humanis, perencanaan pembangunan Kota Pontianak diarahkan untuk menjawab tantangan iklim sekaligus menjaga keseimbangan antara pertumbuhan ekonomi, keberlanjutan ekologi, dan kesejahteraan manusia.
column17:
Dalam perencanaan keuangan, indikator iklim seperti Indeks Risiko Bencana (IRB), Indeks Ketahanan Daerah, dan target penurunan emisi GRK digunakan sebagai dasar evaluasi. Artinya, penganggaran tidak lagi sekadar menutup belanja rutin, tetapi diarahkan pada program-program yang memiliki kontribusi nyata dalam mengurangi risiko iklim. Misalnya, proyek pembangunan fisik harus diuji dengan kajian lingkungan strategis (KLHS) agar sesuai dengan arah mitigasi dan adaptasi perubahan iklim.

Pemkot juga membuka peluang kerja sama pendanaan. Saat ini, Pontianak mendapat alokasi dana untuk pembangunan SPALD-T melalui program Citywide Inclusive Sanitation Project (CISP) yang didanai oleh Asian Development Bank (ADB) melalui Kementerian PUPR. Anggaran awal pembangunan SPALD-T mencapai Rp1,2 triliun, yang akan dibangun selama beberapa tahap (proses lelang telah dimulai pada tahun 2025) dan sepenuhnya berasal dari ADB.

Selain itu, Pemkot Pontianak menerima Rp260 miliar dari pemerintah pusat dengan skema reimburse, yang akan dipakai untuk revitalisasi TPA Batulayang di Pontianak Utara. Revitalisasi ini mencakup pembangunan fasilitas pengolahan sampah seperti pabrik pengolahan menjadi kompos, gas metana, dan produk bernilai ekonomi, serta sistem pengolahan air lindi.

Tentu APBD juga dikeluarkan untuk mendukung fasilitas lain yang tidak masuk dalam bantuan pusat tersebut.
column18:
Pontianak menghadapi keterbatasan fiskal untuk membiayai proyek rendah karbon. Infrastruktur hijau seperti SPALD-T (Rp1,5 triliun dari ADB) dan revitalisasi TPA Batulayang (Rp260 miliar dari pusat) menunjukkan bahwa pendanaan besar masih sangat bergantung pada pusat atau lembaga donor. Risiko yang muncul adalah keberlanjutan pembiayaan. Apakah APBD mampu menanggung biaya operasional, pemeliharaan, dan edukasi masyarakat setelah proyek selesai?

Transisi ke ekonomi rendah karbon menuntut perubahan perilaku masyarakat dalam mengelola sampah, menggunakan energi, hingga pola transportasi. Tantangan utama adalah rendahnya kesadaran publik terhadap manfaat jangka panjang dibanding kenyamanan jangka pendek. Misalnya, meski ada target pengurangan emisi, kendaraan pribadi tetap mendominasi transportasi di Pontianak. Risiko sosialnya adalah resistensi masyarakat ketika ada kebijakan pembatasan atau regulasi ketat.

Teknologi pemantauan karbon dan sistem informasi masih terbatas. Sebenarnya Pemkot memiliki aplikasi SIPPohon. Aplikasi ini mencatat data seluruh pohon di Pontianak, bahkan sudah diuji coba untuk menghitung potensi serapan karbon masing-masing pohon. Jika digarap serius, SIPPohon bisa menjadi instrumen carbon accounting berbasis ekosistem kota, sekaligus bahan advokasi dalam menarik dana carbon trading atau green financing. Namun, tantangan besar adalah keterbatasan kapasitas SDM, integrasi data lintas dinas, serta keberlanjutan pembaruan data.

Transisi rendah karbon tidak bisa hanya ditopang oleh DLH atau BPBD. Diperlukan koordinasi dengan Dinas PU, Bappeda, Dishub, hingga sektor swasta. Risiko koordinasi adalah tumpang tindih kebijakan atau kurangnya sinergi antara pembangunan infrastruktur fisik dengan kebijakan lingkungan. Tanpa integrasi, kebijakan rendah karbon bisa jadi hanya formalitas tanpa implementasi nyata.

column16: Isu-isu iklim telah memengaruhi perencanaan pembangunan Kota Manado dengan mendorong integrasi aspek mitigasi dan adaptasi ke dalam dokumen perencanaan jangka menengah dan panjang, termasuk RPJMD, RAD-GRK, serta KLHS tematik. Tingginya risiko banjir, longsor, dan abrasi pesisir membuat prioritas pembangunan bergeser dari sekadar pertumbuhan ekonomi menjadi pembangunan berketahanan iklim, yang menekankan pada penguatan tata ruang berbasis daya dukung lingkungan, peningkatan ruang terbuka hijau, rehabilitasi mangrove, serta pengendalian alih fungsi lahan. Infrastruktur perkotaan kini dirancang dengan memperhitungkan kerentanan iklim, misalnya melalui peningkatan kapasitas drainase, pembangunan tanggul pesisir, dan transportasi rendah emisi. Perencanaan sosial-ekonomi juga diarahkan untuk melindungi kelompok rentan yang tinggal di bantaran sungai dan wilayah pesisir, sehingga agenda pembangunan daerah tidak hanya mengejar pertumbuhan, tetapi juga memastikan keberlanjutan dan ketahanan terhadap dampak perubahan iklim.
column17: Isu-isu iklim telah memengaruhi perencanaan keuangan Kota Manado karena meningkatnya kebutuhan anggaran untuk penanggulangan banjir, longsor, dan abrasi pesisir yang secara rutin menggerus alokasi APBD, sehingga mengurangi ruang fiskal bagi program pembangunan lainnya. Peristiwa banjir bandang 2014, misalnya, menimbulkan kerugian besar pada infrastruktur, perumahan, dan layanan publik sehingga pemerintah daerah terpaksa melakukan realokasi anggaran darurat. Selain itu, biaya pemeliharaan drainase, penanganan sampah, serta pemulihan pasca bencana terus meningkat, sementara investasi jangka panjang untuk infrastruktur hijau, transportasi berkelanjutan, dan ketahanan pesisir juga harus direncanakan. Hal ini membuat pemerintah kota perlu menyeimbangkan antara pembiayaan adaptasi jangka pendek dan strategi mitigasi jangka panjang, sambil mencari dukungan dari dana pusat, kemitraan swasta, dan potensi akses ke pendanaan iklim internasional.\n
column18: Risiko yang dihadapi Kota Manado dalam transisi menuju ekonomi rendah karbon terutama terkait dengan ketergantungan tinggi pada energi fosil di sektor transportasi dan rumah tangga, yang dapat menimbulkan biaya sosial-ekonomi jika terjadi kenaikan harga BBM atau pembatasan pasokan. Industri kecil dan menengah serta pelaku usaha informal berisiko terdampak karena keterbatasan modal dan teknologi untuk beralih ke praktik produksi yang lebih efisien dan ramah lingkungan. Sektor transportasi publik dan logistik juga menghadapi tantangan investasi besar untuk modernisasi armada rendah emisi. Selain itu, keterbatasan kapasitas fiskal daerah dapat memperlambat implementasi infrastruktur hijau, sementara jika adaptasi kebijakan dilakukan terlalu cepat tanpa dukungan subsidi atau insentif, hal ini berpotensi memperburuk beban ekonomi masyarakat berpenghasilan rendah. Di sisi lain, risiko regulasi dan reputasi juga muncul jika Kota Manado gagal memenuhi target penurunan emisi sesuai komitmen nasional, yang dapat mengurangi peluang memperoleh akses pendanaan iklim dan investasi berkelanjutan.

column16: climate-related issues have significantly influenced our jurisdiction's master and development planning processes. Rising temperatures, increased rainfall variability, and more frequent extreme weather events have required the integration of climate resilience and sustainability into key planning documents, such as the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMD) and annual work plans (RKPD).\n\nWe have incorporated climate risk assessments into spatial planning (RTRW) to identify vulnerable areas and ensure that land use aligns with environmental carrying capacity. Development priorities now include green infrastructure, nature-based solutions, and emission reduction strategies through local climate action plans (e.g., RAD-GRK or RAD-API). Furthermore, budget allocations increasingly reflect climate adaptation and disaster risk reduction efforts.
column17:
Climate-related issues have increasingly influenced our jurisdiction's financial planning processes. Budget allocations now prioritize programs that enhance climate resilience, such as flood mitigation infrastructure, reforestation, early warning systems, and disaster response.

Financial planning has also integrated climate adaptation and mitigation measures into sectoral budgeting through performance-based budgeting and climate budget tagging (CBT). This allows us to track expenditures related to climate actions and align them with national and global climate commitments.

In addition, we have started exploring access to external climate finance sources such as the Green Climate Fund (GCF) and multilateral donor support. These efforts are aimed at closing the funding gap for climate action and ensuring that financial planning supports a low-carbon and climate-resilient development pathway.
column18:
The transition to a low-carbon economy presents several risks to our jurisdiction, particularly in sectors that are currently dependent on fossil fuels or carbon-intensive practices. Key risks include:

Economic Disruption: Industries such as manufacturing, transportation, and energy may face increased operational costs due to stricter emissions standards, carbon pricing, or the need to adopt cleaner technologies.

Employment Impact: Workers in traditional sectors such as coal, diesel-based transport, or unsustainable agriculture may be affected by job displacement without proper reskilling or transition programs.

Infrastructure Adjustment Costs: Significant investment will be needed to upgrade public infrastructure (e.g., energy systems, public transport, waste management) to align with low-carbon standards.

Limited Institutional Capacity: There may be gaps in technical expertise, regulatory frameworks, and financial resources required to manage and accelerate the transition effectively.

Social Resistance: Without adequate public awareness and stakeholder engagement, low-carbon policies could face resistance from communities or businesses that perceive them as burdensome or inequitable.

To address these risks, our jurisdiction is developing inclusive transition strategies that balance environmental goals with economic and social resilience.

In 2016 Dane County voluntarily assumed leadership for countywide climate action when the Dane County Executive created the Office of Energy & Climate Change and charged the office with creating a countywide climate action plan (CAP). The Office convened diverse stakeholders (local municipalities, businesses, environmental and social justice advocates, farmers and the University) and created a CAP that aims to reduce absolute countywide emissions in half by 2030, address the equity and justice issues associated with our fossil fuel economy, increase economic, health and ecosystem benefits, reduce the rural-urban divide, and increase countywide resilience to climate change. Dane County issued the CAP in 2020 with unanimous support from the County Board. Additionally, more than 50 local entities have also signed on as supporters of the CAP (see https://daneclimateaction.org/climate-action-plan/CAP-Supporters). In the CAP we lay out specific climate goals based on climate modelling and commit to reducing countywide emissions in half by 2030 and achieving carbon neutrality by 2050. Note that this is an absolute reduction in a county with 1-2% annual population growth, which means our goal in per capita terms is a 60% reduction per capita by 2030. 

Dane County - like all Wisconsin counties - lacks legislative authority to compel climate action. We cannot update building codes or collect funds for regional transit, for example. We can, however, lead by example in reducing the emissions from county operations and assist public and private partners in reducing duce their emissions. Since completing the Climate Action Plan in 2020 we have done both, reducing Scope 1 and 2 emissions from County operations by 60% since 2020 while promoting countywide action. In late 2022, for example, we leaned into the federal Inflation Reduction Act by creating new website resources and speaking to dozens of groups about ways to leverage federal dollars to accelerate local action. (See https://daneclimateaction.org/what-you-can-do/federal-funding for more on those efforts.)

In addition, as the entity that coordinates countywide emergency management, Dane County has substantial jurisdiction relative to climate disasters, like flooding. In 2021 and 2022 our Emergency Management Services collaborated with local governments to update our Natural Hazard Mitigation Plan with a special focus on climate change and equity considerations. FEMA approved the plan in December 2022.

Further, our Land & Water Resources team are actively engaged in a variety of strategies to mitigate flooding and protect water quality. Many of the land management practices (such as converting farm land back to prairie) have substantial climate benefits in addition to the water quality benefits.

Finally, Dane County Madison Public Health has an Environmental Department that has been active in highlighting and addressing the local health risks associated with climate change. The County also leads cross-jurisdictional efforts to respond to both high heat and extreme cold events; again, these issues are exacerbated by climate change.

According to the Yale Climate Opinion Maps, more people are concerned about climate change in Dane County than anywhere else in Wisconsin. That creates an unofficial mandate for Dane County to be proactive both in reducing emissions and in responding to the changes already baked into our local climate.
column16:
As a Wisconsin county we have limited authority relative to master planning. Under Wisconsin statute, cities and villages have the planning authority within their boundaries and townships can opt out of county planning and set their own priorities. So although we have a holistic view of ongoing master planning processes, we have limited authority to enact comprehensive planning in support of climate action.

That said, Dane County has taken a leadership role in flood mitigation, a major climate issue in our area. In the last few years we have made several strategic land purchases where we were able to purchase farmland prone to flooding rather than watching it be purchased for development. By returning these lands to native prairies in lieu of parking lots, we are mitigating climate impacts in a substantial way. We are currently working to quantify the ecosystem benefits of these strategic land purchases.

Additionally, as noted above, in 2021 and 2022 our Emergency Management Services collaborated with local governments to update our Natural Hazard Mitigation Plan with a special focus on climate change and equity considerations. FEMA approved the plan in December 2022.

The Capital Area Regional Planning Commission (CARPC), which is primarily funded through Dane County, issued a 2050 Regional Development Framework in 2022 that emphasizes planning consistent with climate action priorities. Again, though, local adherence to this plan is optional. More details at https://www.capitalarearpc.org/community-regional-development/regional-development-plan-update/.

Additionally, Dane County has invested millions of dollars in improving water flow through lakes within the County. Recent extreme rainfall events caused flash flooding and also lake level flooding because water flowed into area lakes more quickly than it could flow downstream. After identifying this issue the County created a plan for dredging the waterways between lakes to expedite water flow.

Relative to other areas—like regional transit and building codes—our authority is limited because state statute forbids county or municipal action.
column17:
In the summer of 2018 Dane County experienced two '1,000 year' floods (prior to that we had one in 2008). The largest of these extreme precipitation events on August 20th, 2018, resulted in more than 15 inches of rain in certain villages in western Dane County. That storm resulted in more than $150 million in damages and the loss of one life, and required more than 80 emergency rescues to prevent additional loss of life. In the last few years Dane County has invested tens of millions of dollars to reduce risks associated with these types of flooding events. These investments included dredging efforts to increase water flow through the Yahara River of lakes (which prevents lake level flooding associated with flash flooding in rain events) and increasing our Emergency Management resources.

In 2022 Dane County Emergency Management worked with local jurisdictions to update our joint Natural Disaster Hazard Mitigation Plan with a special emphasis on the changing natural disaster risks associated with climate change. As part of that planning effort, Dane County and local municipalities have identified a variety of potential projects to reduce climate risks. Following FEMA approval of the plan, Dane County and local municipalities began investing in those climate resilience efforts
column18:
Dane County anticipates relatively few risks associated with the transition to a low carbon economy. Our local economy includes multiple bio-tech industries, a major research university, other white collar industries and substantial dairy operations. With no fossil fuel production in our area and typically the lowest unemployment rates in the state, individuals with fossil fuel jobs have good options to pursue other employment, including in the clean energy sector. In addition, our local electric utilities have committed to providing clean electricity in the future and are actively engaged in that transition.

One potential risk with the transition to a low carbon economy is in implementing this transition inequitably across the county. Climate change disproportionately impacts people of color and socially vulnerable communities. Dane County needs to account for this discrepancy by providing increased support for these communities to ensure equitable access and opportunities to make this transition.

However, perhaps the greatest risk for Dane County is that the State of Wisconsin would enact additional legislation pre-empting about ability to make local progress transitioning to a clean energy economy. In recent years the state legislature has enacted various kinds of pre-emption that make it more difficult for local municipalities to pursue a clean energy future and, it is feasible that more impediments might be forthcoming.

Antalya Metropolitan Municipality joined the Covenant of Mayors (CoM) in 2013, committing to systematic climate action. In 2019, Antalya became the first metropolitan municipality in Türkiye to prepare a Sustainable Energy Action Plan (SEAP) following the CoM methodology, with a target to reduce GHG emissions by 40% by 2030 from a 2019 baseline.
In 2020, the municipal council established the Climate Change and Clean Energy Directorate to coordinate mitigation and adaptation projects across departments. In 2022, the Climate Change and Zero Waste (CCZW) Department was created, integrating the directorate and expanding the city's mandate to include zero waste, circular economy, and broader environmental governance. Oversight mechanisms ensure that climate considerations are embedded in strategic planning, budgeting, and major capital investment decisions, with regular reporting to the municipal council and relevant committees.
In 2022, the SEAP was updated into a Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plan (SECAP), aligning with Türkiye's national net-zero target and NDCs and committing Antalya to carbon neutrality by 2050. The plan sets out sectoral mitigation actions, resilience-building adaptation measures, and annual monitoring requirements.
Antalya's governance framework is reinforced by national and local legislation: The Türkiye Climate Law (No. 7552, July 2025) mandates integration of climate into all levels of decision-making, while the forthcoming Local Climate Change Action Plan Regulation (YİDEP) will require municipalities to prepare participatory, science-based local plans consistent with the national net-zero pathway. Locally, the Municipal Council's Environmental Board—unique in Türkiye—provides a formal platform for stakeholder participation in climate and environmental decision-making.
In 2022, Antalya became the first municipality and public institution in Türkiye to receive the “Climate Friendly Organization Certificate” from the Turkish Standards Institution (TSE) following renewable energy integration and efficiency upgrades in municipal buildings. In 2023, the Antalya Water and Wastewater Administration (ASAT) earned the same certificate, extending the city's climate commitments to utility services.
The CCZW department leads integrated programs in renewable energy, energy efficiency, sustainable mobility, water management, marine pollution prevention, climate-resilient agriculture, biodiversity protection, waste reduction, and public education. It coordinates projects with national agencies, universities, and international partners, embedding climate risk and resilience into sectoral policies.
In 2024, Antalya contributed to the AFAD-coordinated City Disaster Risk Reduction and Climate Adaptation Action Plan, which builds on the 2022 Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction Plan (IRAP) to address heatwaves, droughts, wildfires, and floods. These plans strengthen institutional roles, define monitoring responsibilities, and integrate climate risk into land-use, infrastructure, and emergency planning.
Between 2019-2024, Antalya implemented award-winning climate and environmental projects, documented in the “We Promised to our Nature” publishing series, earning 24 local, national, and international awards for excellence in renewable energy, sustainable urban transport, waste management, marine protection, and awareness-raising.
Antalya's climate governance approach is long-term, rule-based, participatory, and science-driven, ensuring that climate action is a core element of municipal governance, safeguarding the rights of present and future generations.
column16:
Antalya, located in the Mediterranean Basin, is highly vulnerable to climate change impacts including rising temperatures, prolonged droughts, more frequent heatwaves, floods, and extreme weather events. These hazards directly affect the city's main economic sectors—tourism and agriculture—while also threatening infrastructure, water resources, biodiversity, and public health. For example, tourism, which accounts for a large share of Antalya's economy, faces risks from heat stress, wildfire smoke, and water shortages, while agriculture is impacted by shifting precipitation patterns, salinization, and pest outbreaks.
Recognizing these risks, climate change adaptation and mitigation are systematically integrated into the city's master and development planning processes. The Western Mediterranean Development Agency (BAKA) TR61 Regional Plan (2014-2023) set a framework for regional resilience, prioritizing multimodal and maritime transport integration, sustainable land use, and disaster risk reduction. Locally, the Antalya Metropolitan Municipality's 2020-2024 Strategic Plan embedded climate-related priorities across multiple strategic objectives:
Strategic Goal 9: Guide social and economic development while preserving the city's natural, historical, and cultural assets, including disaster preparedness (Target 9.5).
Strategic Goal 10: Create a green, healthy, and nature-respecting city (Targets 10.1-10.4 on green spaces, environmental health, waste management, and public health improvements).
Strategic Goal 11: Expand renewable energy resources (Target 11.6).
Strategic Goal 12: Strengthen agricultural infrastructure, protect resources, and raise producer awareness (Target 12.2).
Strategic Goal 13: Develop safe, integrated, and future-ready public transportation with a focus on rail systems.
The upcoming 2025-2029 Strategic Plan further strengthens climate integration, aligning with the Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plan (SECAP) and Türkiye's net-zero 2050 target. Climate vulnerability assessments and disaster risk data—such as from the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction Plan (IRAP) and the City Disaster Risk Reduction and Climate Adaptation Action Plan (2024)—inform spatial planning, infrastructure investments, and emergency preparedness strategies.
At the national level, the Türkiye Climate Law (No. 7552, July 2025) now provides a legal mandate for integrating climate action into local planning, requiring alignment with national net-zero targets, annual reporting, and participatory planning processes. The forthcoming Local Climate Change Action Plan Regulation (YİDEP)—for which Antalya is selected as one of the pilot cities—will set the operational framework for municipal climate plans, ensuring science-based and community-driven approaches are embedded into local development strategies.
In practice, these frameworks have driven climate-friendly urban initiatives, including: renewable energy projects in municipal facilities; expansion of bicycle and rail transit networks; flood-resilient drainage systems; wildfire prevention zones; climate-smart agricultural programs; and marine pollution control. Climate risks are also considered in zoning, coastal protection, and water management master plans.
Between 2019-2024, the municipality implemented flagship climate and environmental projects documented in the “We Promised to our Nature” book series, earning 24 awards at local, national, and international levels. These achievements reflect a governance model that sees climate change not as a separate agenda but as a cross-cutting driver shaping the city's spatial, economic, and social development strategies.
column17:
Antalya Metropolitan Municipality is only starting to develop its financial capacity for climate-related issues. The municipality budgets for its own expenses, but solving the climate-related problems requires external funding, both nationally and internationally.
National external sources are looking at ministerial programs, AFAD-supported risk reduction, and project-based grants. International, or competitive funding include grants, loans, and technical assistance potential by programs like World Bank, EU Covenant of Mayors, ICLEI, UNDP, Interreg MED, Horizon Europe (PRIMA call and others EU calls), and other multilateral climate finance mechanisms. The international supporting funding has been necessary for climate issues related to floods, heat waves, droughts, wildfire prevention projects, marine pollution, and public health risk projects. The international external funding sources are important to the realization of the SEAP (2019) and SECAP (2022), both development and implementation; without these external funding resources the realization of the SEAP and SECAP projects would not have been possible. The participating level of external funding helped the municipality with project inputs such as emission inventories, emissions reduction targets, and early action to adapt to climate-related issues. 
The challenges of aligning climate-related priorities with the municipality's financial planning is taken into account in the climate-supporting aims and declarations in the 2024 to 2028 Strategic Plans for the Antalya Metropolitan Municipality, such as ultimately reaching the carbon neutral goal by 2050. The annual performance programming, is the connecting piece allowing for municipal strategic objectives to inform the budgetary allocations of mitigation, adaptation, and environmental protection.
Decision-making is increasingly factoring in cost-benefit analysis into decision making. Coastal protection is an area of established investments for Antalya, supported by longer term planning, monitoring, and ongoing projects. In other areas, such as wildfire mitigation and hardening of public infrastructure for extreme heat; this approach is newer, but is beginning to incorporate the allocation of funding through earmarking its priority and beginning to shape project design. This incremental thinking for prevention is to avoid the need for more costly recovery initiated by natural disasters.
column18:
Antalya is Türkiye's 5th largest city, with rapid population growth and inward migration leading to increased energy demand, transport demand, and pressures on urban infrastructure. Collectively, these socio-economic pressures generate transition risk in the move to a low carbon economy including: 
Infrastructure and technology dependence: Responsible for many low carbon technologies and components (for example, renewable energy technologies and electric vehicle infrastructure) not being produced domestically leaves projects exposed to foreign exchange changes and import prices. 
Financial limitations: Municipal cash budgets are often too limited, with challenges in potential budget transfers from the central government, high inflation rates, and volatility in national currency limit the potential for substantial investments in large scale low carbon infrastructure and projects. 
Awareness and behaviour: Educational attainment is average, but even with that, public awareness and buy-in to low carbon sustainable practices is very limited which slows mitigation measures including sustainable transport, less waste generation, and energy efficiency. 
Urban development pressures: Rapid urban sprawl and development risk locking-in high carbon infrastructure for decades if new urban development does not have low carbon requirements. 
Market and operational risks: Uncertainty in energy price volatility, and determining the trajectory of national policy and aspirations, as well as uncertainty around the timing, manner, and extent of climate finance makes it difficult to determine the feasibility of a project. 
These transition risks highlight a need for stable funding mechanisms, establishment of capacity locally, as well as locally designed and deployed low-carbon technologies deemed feasible and low bilateral exchange risks. All help to support the journey towards Antalya's 2050 carbon neutrality goal.

column15:
Kadıköy Municipality ensures oversight of climate-related issues through integrated planning, internal coordination mechanisms, and performance monitoring systems.

A dedicated unit within the Climate Change and Zero Waste Directorate coordinates climate-related initiatives. Climate risks and opportunities are considered during the formulation of the municipality's 5-year Strategic Plan, most recently the 2025-2029 plan. This plan incorporates climate mitigation and adaptation targets under a dedicated strategic axis (A3), with resilience mainstreamed across all other domains including urban planning, infrastructure, and public health.

The municipality regularly conducts interdepartmental workshops (e.g., SECAP Monitoring Workshop) to evaluate progress on climate targets and gather updates from relevant departments. These processes are supported by 40+ performance indicators covering emissions reduction, green space, water management, energy use, urban heat island effects, and public health. As of 2020, 23 out of 25 SECAP actions were under implementation.

Progress is reviewed annually through performance programs and activity reports submitted to the municipal council. Budget allocations are tracked to ensure that climate-related investments are aligned with the municipality's 2030 targets (e.g., 40% emissions reduction). A total budget of approximately 3.1 billion TL was planned for climate action under SECAP.

In addition, climate-related issues are integrated into spatial planning and risk management processes based on the Kadıköy 2030 Resilience Vision and its data-driven urban situation analysis. External stakeholder input is regularly gathered via public consultations and thematic workshops involving academia, NGOs, and residents.

These structures and practices ensure continuous oversight and integration of climate priorities into Kadıköy Municipality's governance and investment decisions.
column16:
Climate-related risks and opportunities have significantly shaped Kadıköy Municipality's master and development planning, with a focus on both adaptation and mitigation. Climate action has been embedded into the municipality's 2025-2029 Strategic Plan, aligned with its Kadıköy 2030 Resilience Vision. These planning frameworks consider medium- to long-term time horizons, particularly through 2030 and beyond.

Key areas of influence include:

Urban infrastructure: Climate change adaptation is central to planning for resilient infrastructure. Strategic Goal A2H3 focuses on improving disaster and emergency preparedness, including climate-related risks such as flooding and heatwaves.

Land use and spatial planning: The Kadıköy 2030 Situation Analysis informed the identification of vulnerable zones (e.g., aging building stock, flood-prone areas), which directly influenced zoning, building reinforcement, and green corridor strategies.

Green infrastructure: In response to urban heat island effects, planning prioritizes green space creation and ecological corridors (A3H4), linked to cooling and biodiversity objectives.

Mobility and energy: Development planning includes sustainable mobility and clean energy systems, supported by measures from the SECAP to reduce emissions by 40% by 2030.

Public health and social equity: Climate vulnerability mapping informs adaptation strategies for at-risk populations (elderly, low-income groups), especially under increasing heat stress and air pollution concerns.

The most substantial strategic decision influenced by climate-related risks was the integration of a resilience lens across all four strategic development pillars: social, ecological, urban, and institutional. This has transformed planning from siloed infrastructure development to a holistic, climate-aware governance model.

Additionally, the Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plan (SECAP) and its associated monitoring framework ensure that every major development investment considers climate impacts. For example, the ~3.1 billion TL climate investment portfolio was prioritized and sequenced based on emissions data and vulnerability assessments.

In summary, Kadıköy Municipality's development planning is now directly guided by climate science, participatory scenario analysis, and resilience-building principles across all sectors, covering a planning horizon through 2030 and setting a foundation for longer-term goals toward 2050.
column17:
Kadıköy Municipality has integrated climate-related risks and opportunities into both its capital and operational budgeting.

A total of 3.1 billion TL has been allocated for climate-related projects under the Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plan (SECAP) until 2030. These include investments in renewable energy, sustainable transport, green spaces, and climate-resilient infrastructure (e.g. flood prevention and building retrofits).

Operational budgets now also include:

Monitoring of emissions and climate indicators,

Maintenance of green and resilient infrastructure,

Public awareness and staff training.

Kadıköy has also improved access to national and international funding (e.g. EU IPA funds) by aligning its plans with climate goals and maintaining strong project tracking.

In summary, climate issues now directly shape financial priorities in Kadıköy, with planning focused on long-term resilience and sustainability.
column18:
Kadıköy Municipality faces several risks related to the transition to a low-carbon economy:

Regulatory risks: National climate regulations may change quickly, creating uncertainty for local planning and requiring costly updates to infrastructure.

Technology risks: New low-carbon technologies can be expensive and complex to implement. There is a risk of falling behind due to limited technical capacity or fast-changing innovations.

Market risks: The demand for green materials and services may increase prices or cause delays in projects.

Reputational risks: As a municipality known for climate leadership, failure to meet public goals or report progress could damage trust among citizens and partners.

Capacity risks: Limited staff, expertise, or coordination can slow down climate action.

Kadıköy is addressing these risks through long-term planning (SECAP, Strategic Plan 2025-2029), but some challenges depend on national and global developments.

column15: Located at the west coast of Turkey on the Aegean Sea, Izmir belongs to the broader region of Southeast Europe, and is one of the key port cities in the Eastern Mediterranean. Izmir province stretches over an area of 12.000 km2 and comprises 30 city districts, 11 of which are situated in the metropolitan area. With the advantages of its climate and geographic location, the city has become home to different civilizations and cultures throughout its 8500 years of history. Izmir is the one of the historical cultural centers in the world, where different cultures, lifestyles and beliefs have lived together for thousands of years IMM holds a very important place in local administration organisation of Izmir, being the third largest city in Turkey with a population of around 4.5 million people. IMM is responsible for wide variety of areas including social projects, environment, IT, transportation, energy, natural resources supply, infrastructure, planning and development, community services, vocational education, health, culture, tourism, etc. It is one of the rare cities that can host many different sectors such as industry, tourism, and agriculture at the same time. Izmir also has thermal power plants, oil refineries and renewable energy systems. Izmir is one of the prominent cities in terms of the use and development of renewable energy resources with its geographical location, ecological structure, development in agriculture and industry. The city has actively pursued climate neutrality through several action plans aligned with European Union standards, such as SEAP (Sustainable Energy Action Plan), SECAP (Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plan), and GCAP (Green City Action Plan). As a signatory of the Covenant of Mayors, Izmir began climate change initiatives in 2015. Successfully achieving a 20% reduction target by 2020, Izmir prioritizes nature-based solutions in its climate efforts. As a continuation of the process, SECAP and GCAP were prepared. It was the first city in Turkey to prepare GCAP. İzmir has set a target of 40% greenhouse gas emission reduction in 2030 with SECAP. As a next step, IMM participated in the “Cities Compete with Zero” program, which aims to achieve net zero carbon emissions by 2050. In line with all those efforts, Izmir is also involved in the EU's Climate-Neutral and Smart Cities Mission under the Horizon Europe Program. Eventually, in March 2024, Izmir received the prestigious EU Mission Label, along with 22 cities in Europe. This award represents an important milestone in the city's work on sustainability. Izmir is also one of the 311 regions and local authorities that signed the Mission Charter within the EU Mission of Climate Change Adaptation that committing to support local and regional efforts to adapt to climate change
column16: Over the last decade, Izmir has experienced severe forest fires, floods, and other climate-related disasters, which have directly shaped the city's master and development planning. Climate risks are now systematically integrated into spatial planning processes to ensure resilient urban growth. As a result, water management (treatment, supply, and infrastructure), waste management, renewable energy transformation, and sustainable transportation projects have been prioritized and accelerated in line with İzmir's Climate Action Plan.\nİzmir was selected for the EU's Climate-Neutral and Smart Cities Mission, bringing forward its net zero target from 2050 to 2030. Furthermore, İzmir is also part of the EU Mission on Adaptation to Climate Change, ensuring that adaptation measures such as green infrastructure, ecosystem-based solutions, and disaster risk reduction are embedded into development planning.\n
column17: IMM has identified the estimated costs of some mitigation and adaptation actions in its SECAP. However, climate-related events such as floods, heatwaves, and forest fires have required additional emergency expenditures, leading to a reallocation of municipal resources. Combined with the pandemic, the global economic crisis, inflation, and rising project costs, these pressures have constrained IMM's financial planning and highlighted the need for external funding.\n\n

O Município de Francisco Morato tem demonstrado comprometimento com a agenda climática e com a supervisão de problemas decorrentes das mudanças do clima por meio de diferentes instrumentos institucionais e normativos.

Em primeiro lugar, destaca-se a adesão à Agenda 2030 da ONU, que reflete o alinhamento da gestão municipal aos Objetivos de Desenvolvimento Sustentável (ODS). Tal medida reforça o compromisso com políticas públicas integradas e com a implementação de ações voltadas à sustentabilidade, à mitigação de impactos ambientais e à promoção da resiliência urbana.

A administração municipal também conta com a Secretaria de Habitação, Meio Ambiente, Clima e Energia, órgão responsável pela coordenação e implementação de políticas locais voltadas ao enfrentamento das questões ambientais e climáticas. Essa estrutura administrativa possibilita uma abordagem transversal, que integra o planejamento urbano, a gestão ambiental e a adaptação climática.

Adicionalmente, foi instituída no município a Comissão dos ODS's, instância colegiada destinada a acompanhar, articular e monitorar o cumprimento das metas relacionadas à Agenda 2030, garantindo a participação social e a integração intersetorial nas ações locais.

Por fim, merece destaque a elaboração do Plano Municipal de Adaptação e Resiliência à Mudança do Clima, documento que sistematiza diagnósticos, metas e estratégias para enfrentar os efeitos adversos das alterações climáticas, promovendo tanto a mitigação de riscos quanto o fortalecimento da capacidade adaptativa do território e da população.

Assim, observa-se que a supervisão de problemas relacionados ao clima em Francisco Morato está estruturada em políticas públicas de planejamento, instrumentos normativos e instâncias de gestão específicas, em consonância com compromissos nacionais e internacionais de sustentabilidade.
column16: O Plano Diretor Municipal dedica um capítulo específico às questões ambientais e climáticas. O Capítulo I - Da Dimensão Ambiental (Art. 9º) estabelece diretrizes voltadas à sustentabilidade, às condições de saneamento, à oferta de energia, à produção e ao consumo responsáveis, à educação ambiental e ao controle das mudanças climáticas. Essa previsão normativa assegura que a pauta climática esteja incorporada ao principal instrumento de planejamento territorial do município.
column17:
Os problemas relacionados às mudanças do clima têm gerado impactos significativos no planejamento financeiro do Município de Francisco Morato, demandando a alocação de recursos específicos e a reestruturação das prioridades orçamentárias.

Em primeiro lugar, eventos extremos como enchentes, deslizamentos e períodos de estiagem recorrentes exigem investimentos constantes em infraestrutura de drenagem, contenção de encostas, recuperação de áreas degradadas e obras emergenciais de mitigação de riscos, impactando diretamente o orçamento público.

Paralelamente, a necessidade de adequação às diretrizes da Agenda 2030 e do Plano Municipal de Adaptação e Resiliência à Mudança do Clima implica a previsão de recursos para ações de longo prazo, como programas de educação ambiental, projetos de eficiência energética, incentivo a construções sustentáveis e expansão de sistemas de saneamento básico, com enfoque preventivo.

A existência da Secretaria de Habitação, Meio Ambiente, Clima e Energia e da Comissão dos ODS's também influencia a gestão financeira, uma vez que tais estruturas administrativas requerem dotação orçamentária própria para executar e monitorar políticas públicas voltadas à sustentabilidade e ao controle das mudanças climáticas.

Adicionalmente, a previsão normativa no Plano Diretor Municipal, que inclui o Capítulo I - Da Dimensão Ambiental (Art. 9º), reforça a obrigatoriedade de considerar aspectos ambientais e climáticos no planejamento territorial e financeiro, assegurando que os investimentos municipais estejam alinhados a critérios de sustentabilidade.

Assim, observa-se que os impactos climáticos impõem à jurisdição a necessidade de um planejamento financeiro orientado tanto para ações imediatas de resposta a eventos críticos, quanto para estratégias de médio e longo prazo de adaptação e resiliência, o que resulta em maior complexidade na gestão orçamentária e na priorização de gastos públicos.
column18:
A transição para uma economia de baixo carbono, embora necessária e estratégica para o enfrentamento da crise climática, envolve riscos que podem impactar diretamente a gestão pública municipal. No caso de Francisco Morato, destacam-se:

Risco Social e de Desigualdade

Adoção de tarifas, tributos ou custos associados à transição (como substituição de equipamentos e uso de energias renováveis) pode gerar exclusão social, afetando famílias de baixa renda que já vivem em situação de vulnerabilidade.

A falta de empregos formais e de qualificação profissional dificulta a inserção da população nas novas cadeias produtivas verdes.

Risco Econômico e de Empregabilidade

Como a economia local é centrada no comércio e não na indústria, há poucos setores produtivos capazes de absorver investimentos em tecnologias limpas ou gerar empregos qualificados vinculados à transição energética.

A pressão por formalização pode aumentar a informalidade e agravar o desemprego, caso não sejam criadas alternativas acessíveis de capacitação e inserção laboral.

Risco Territorial e Habitacional

A elevada taxa de ocupações irregulares, inclusive em áreas de preservação permanente (APPs) e zonas de risco, dificulta a implementação de infraestrutura energética sustentável (como redes de energia solar distribuída ou melhorias de eficiência).

Regularização fundiária atua sobre regime de alta demanda, o que impede o acesso rápido dessas populações a programas de financiamento ou subsídios de transição energética.

Risco de Planejamento Urbano

A pequena extensão territorial combinada com alta densidade populacional limita áreas para instalação de equipamentos energéticos (como usinas solares, centrais de armazenamento ou ecoparques), aumentando a dependência de energia importada.

Conflitos pelo uso do solo podem ser agravados se áreas de preservação ou de risco forem pressionadas para abrigar estruturas energéticas.

Risco Fiscal e de Capacidade de Investimento

Municípios com economia fragilizada e baixa arrecadação enfrentam dificuldades para captar recursos e cofinanciar projetos de transição energética.

Dependência de fundos estaduais e federais pode atrasar ou restringir a implementação de medidas locais.

Risco Institucional e de Governança

A alta demanda do corpo técnico-administrativa e a necessidade de múltiplas articulações intersetoriais podem comprometer a eficácia da transição.

Resistência política e social pode surgir, especialmente se as medidas forem percebidas como onerosas ou excludentes para a população mais pobre.

Risco Ambiental Indireto

A pressão por adaptação rápida sem planejamento pode gerar impactos colaterais, como descarte inadequado de equipamentos antigos, aumento de passivos ambientais e ocupação irregular de áreas sensíveis para projetos energéticos.

The Municipality of Sintra intends to develop a transition plan and contribute to mitigating and adapting to climate change and improving its response to current and future vulnerabilities. The municipality is strongly committed to promoting a more sustainable development, with lower environmental impacts and better adapted to Climate Change, and has developed several initiatives in this direction.
Sintra Council's Strategic Plan in the face of Climate Change (Plano Estratégico do Concelho de Sintra face às Alterações Climáticas) was developed in 2009. The areas/sectors to be covered by the risk and vulnerability assessment were identified by taking as reference a prior socio-economic characterisation of the municipality, a framework for national strategies with impacts on adaptation to climate change and other reference methodologies.
More recently, is under implementation the Plan Metropolitan Plan of Adaptation to Climate Change of the Metropolitan Area of Lisbon 2019 (PMAAC AML), were the municipality of Sintra is included. The Bioclimatic scenario building consisted of collecting and processing future climate information (projections), using several models that allow the production of regional climate scenarios. An evaluation and scenario of bioclimatic comfort was also carried out, considering the main climatic variables with a potentially harmful effect on human health, namely heat waves, cold waves and human thermal comfort. The risk evolution was also analyzed for the main impacts associated with climate events for the nine sectors of PMAAC-AML: agriculture and forests; biodiversity and landscape; economy - industry, tourism and services; energy; water resources; human health; safety of people and property; transport and communications; coastal areas.
In 2023 Sintra developed it's Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plan (Sintra SECAP 2023), an integrated climate plan addressing mitigation and adaptation, in line with national and European strategic guidelines. 
Within the framework of Sintra SECAP 2023, a number of climate sustainability measures have been defined, the implementation of which will make it possible to fulfil the commitment made when signing the Covenant of Mayors for Climate and Energy.
Also, in 2022, the municipality was selected by the European Commission to take part in the
Mission to Adapt to Climate Change, thus recognising the path that the municipality has planned for a resilient and towards a resilient and sustainable future.
column16: The Sintra Municipal Master Plan proposes clear measures to enable the territory to mitigate and adapt to climate change, some of which have already begun, such as: the creation of a cycling and pedestrian network; the construction of urban parks and incentives to increase and maintain forests to combat greenhouse gases; the promotion of green corridors and maintenance of wetland systems; hydraulic utilisation for irrigation; an increase in the area conditioned to the evolution of cliffs; protection of areas threatened by river floods and marine overtopping, among others.
column17:
The municipal executive defined six strategic objectives (SO) for the municipality, which are materialised in the Municipal Budget, highlighting the intervention and implementation of activities aimed at achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), in their three classic dimensions: economic, social and environmental.
Within the scope of climate action, we highlight SO III - Make Sintra a benchmark in environmental preservation and respect for the requirements inherent to the heritage of humanity, applying the sustainability measures necessary to achieve this objective, namely. 
In conjunction with the municipal planning elements (PDM, Sintra SECAP 2023, among others), the Municipal Budget includes the items needed to implement clear measures to mitigate and adapt to climate change in the municipality.
Within the scope of Sintra SECAP 2023, the investment needed to implement the various mitigation and adaptation measures planned was identified, as well as the resources, schemes and financial mechanisms available, in order to plan and ensure their implementation, both in terms of defining municipal investment priorities and in terms of attracting external investment and obtaining funding. Whenever possible, the municipality endeavours to leverage private sector investment, promoting synergies and guaranteeing secure financing.
column18:
The transition to a low-carbon economy presents many risks and opportunities for the municipality: the risks create demand for decarbonisation solutions which, in turn, create opportunities to offer these solutions.
The risks result from:
. regulatory actions, aimed at restricting actions that contribute to the adverse effects of climate change or promoting mitigation and adaptation to climate change;
. technological innovation, which is essential to introduce improvements or innovations to support and drive the transition to a low-carbon and energy-efficient economic system;
. community perception, which is essential for the transition to a low-carbon economy.
. changes in the market, namely changes in the supply and demand of goods, which should boost the availability of products and services with a low carbon footprint (i.e. renewable energies, battery storage, hydrogen market, plant-based proteins, voluntary carbon market, etc.).
. financial, insofar as it is essential to attract extra-municipal financial resources and investment, necessary for the implementation of strategies and respective measures to mitigate and adapt to climate change.

No que toca à ação climática, o Município da Maia tem como visão atingir neutralidade carbónica em 2030 e desenvolver uma capacidade de resiliência do seu território aos riscos e impactes das alterações climáticas.
A necessidade de mitigar as emissões de GEE, nomeadamente as decorrentes da utilização de energia, assim como adaptar o território para os efeitos das alterações climáticas tem vindo a ser plasmada em diversos compromissos internacionais e nacionais com efeito à escala local, como são exemplo o Pacto de Autarcas para o Clima e Energia, subscrito pela Maia em 2017 e reforçado em 2022, e onde o Município se comprometeu a envidar esforços para reduzir em 40% as suas emissões de GEE, até 2030, face a 2008, e atingir a neutralidade carbónica, até 2050, reduzindo em 90% as suas emissões. A fim de materializar este compromisso político, o Município da Maia elaborou o seu Plano de Ação para a Energia Sustentável da Maia 2030 (PAES), assim como, o seu Plano Municipal de Adaptação às Alterações Climáticas (PMAAC) que traduzem, respetivamente, a estratégia maiata em matéria de mitigação e adaptação às alterações climáticas no horizonte 2030. Atualmente, a Maia está a estudar a o objetivo de ir além das metas nacionais e atingir Neutralidade Carbónica até 2030, antecipando a meta de descarbonização nacional prevista para 2045 - 2050. Esta é uma aspiração mais ambiciosa do que as metas estabelecidas pela Lei de Bases do Clima (Lei n.º 98/2021, de 31 de dezembro) que requer que as autoridades locais impulsionem e acelerem a ação climática local ao desenvolverem Planos Municipais de Ação Climática, consolidando instrumentos de política local nestas matérias e definindo as estratégias locais rumo à descarbonização. 

Relativamente à vertente da adaptação, a adoção de uma Estratégia Municipal de Adaptação às Alterações Climáticas (EMAAC) e, consequentemente, de um Plano Municipal de Adaptação às Alterações Climáticas (PMAAC) pretende promover, em todo o território municipal, uma resposta coerente às múltiplas problemáticas relacionadas com as alterações climáticas, através de ações de gestão preventiva
e adaptativa, valorizando o planeamento e sustentabilidade territorial como fatores de resiliência climática, reduzindo as incertezas e antecipando os desafios dos próximos tempos.
Considera-se assim, a necessidade de intervenção face às alterações climáticas no sentido da adaptação local fundamental, sendo encarada na esfera municipal como matéria prioritária, pela inevitabilidade que os seus impactes produzem e continuarão a produzir no território e quotidiano da população. 
Os documentos elaborados na área da adaptação climática têm como visão estratégica a congregação dos contributos que refletem as expectativas da comunidade maiata para o futuro, veiculada pelos agentes-chave locais representados no Workshop Participativo “Adaptação às Alterações Climáticas no Município da Maia”: “Um município capacitado e resiliente na resposta às alterações climáticas, visando a redução da vulnerabilidade do território, através de um diálogo de proximidade com os agentes locais, potenciando a participação cívica.” 
O município da Maia tem também uma visão mais holística, isto é, indo para além para além da problemática do clima. Esta cidade retende ser “amiga, equilibrada e responsável, solidária e inclusiva, realizada e feliz”, um município “focado no caminho do progresso e desenvolvimento, capaz de assegurar confiança no futuro” e ainda espera ser uma referência na Europa no “uso de tecnologias digitais destinadas a promover a mobilidade urbana, a eficiência energética, o acesso à informação, a qualidade dos serviços públicos e privados, e a criação de negócios intensivos em conhecimento”. Esta intenção está contemplada no MAIA 2028 - Plano Estratégico (https://www.cm-maia.pt/cmmaia/uploads/writer_file/document/2878/maia_2028_digital.pdf)e tem quatro objetivos estratégicos principais:
•	Criação de condições de estilos de vida saudáveis;
•	Preservação da natureza e a utilização inteligente dos recursos naturais e energéticos;
•	Atrair investimento gerador de riqueza e de oportunidades de trabalho;
•	Promover a integração e interação social na construção de uma comunidade coesa e sustentável.
column16: A concretização das opções de adaptação preconizadas nas medidas de adaptação (capítulo 8.2) terá de ser enquadrada atempadamente no âmbito dos processos de planeamento territorial e setorial e, consequentemente, na programação de ações e na conceção de projetos no quadro das políticas públicas locais e das competências municipais. As medidas de adaptação através do ordenamento do território devem considerar, entre outros: · Os riscos de inundação, erosão costeira, incêndios, ondas de calor e secas, ponderando os seus impactos face às alterações climáticas e estabelecendo regulamentos ao uso do solo que tenham em consideração a necessária salvaguarda de pessoas e bens; · O design e construção de novos edifícios e planeamento dos espaços públicos que sejam resilientes às alterações climáticas, em especial as ondas de calor; · A valorização dos serviços dos ecossistemas na sua vertente de regulação climática, provisão alimentar e proteção de habitats, destacando-se a relevância de definição e concretização das Estruturas Ecológicas Municipais e Urbanas e a criação de infraestruturas verdes; A promoção de uma gestão eficiente dos recursos hídricos, quer em termos qualitativos quer quantitativos. Por outro lado, o ordenamento do território pode ter um papel importante na adaptação às alterações climáticas, contribuindo para uma adaptação planeada, através dos Instrumentos de Gestão Territorial (IGT), que identificam e harmonizam os vários interesses públicos prosseguidos com expressão territorial, tendo em conta as estratégias de desenvolvimento económico e social, bem como a sustentabilidade e a solidariedade intergeracional na ocupação e utilização do território, e que devem assumir um papel antecipatório e pró-ativo na promoção de uma adaptação robusta através da integração de medidas de adaptação para reduzir os danos e capitalizar as oportunidades associadas às alterações climáticas. Foram assim identificadas, sob a perspetiva do ordenamento do território, as opções que poderão ser implementadas através destes instrumentos, assim como a forma como estas poderão vir a ser associadas aos diferentes elementos que os constituem (conteúdo material e documental). Neste sentido, na tabela seguinte apresenta-se, para cada opção de adaptação identificada como potencialmente concretizável, através dos planos, políticas e regulamentos de âmbito municipal em vigor no município da Maia, um conjunto de formas de integração que deverão ser equacionadas, identificando-se ainda os elementos dos planos que deverão ser alterados para a sua concretização.
column17:
O financiamento das medidas previstas para a adaptação climática é assegurado, quer por fundos próprios do Município, quer pelas linhas externas de financiamento disponíveis, identificadas para cada área de intervenção.
Ao nível municipal, todos os anos é definida verba nas Grandes Opções do Plano relativa à ação climática, considerando-se a priorização da implementação das medidas previstas, nos respetivos planos de ação.
O financiamento externo, por seu turno, está centrado em diversos instrumentos de financiamento (da União Europeia, de fundos nacionais, de instituições financeiras internacionais e outras organizações privadas). 
Destacam-se os principais:
	Programa Life - Subprograma de mitigação e adaptação às alterações Climáticas
Programa de financiamento da União Europeia dedicado ao ambiente e ação climática
O LIFE 2021-2027, constitui um instrumento financeiro para o ambiente e a ação climática, tendo sido estabelecido pelo Regulamento (UE) 2021/783, com vista a contribuir para a transição para uma economia sustentável, circular, energeticamente eficiente, baseada nas energias renováveis, neutra para o clima e resiliente.
	Programa Horizonte 2030 - Programa de financiamento da União Europeia para a investigação e inovação
A sua organização em 5 missões constituem uma novidade do programa de investigação e inovação do Horizonte Europa para o período 2021-2027, das quais se destaca:
•	Missão na área de Adaptação para as alterações climáticas, incluindo a transformação societal;
•	Missão na área da Cidades inteligentes e com impacto neutro no clima
	Fundo Social para a Ação Climática
Com a revisão da ambição para 2030 o âmbito do pacote Fir for 55 será criado o Fundo Social para a Ação climática (FSAC) que pretende reduzir o impacto social do alargamento do regime do Comércio Europeu de Licenças de Emissão (CELE) ao setor do transporte rodoviário e edifícios, sobretudo junto dos mais vulneráveis como famílias, empresas e utilizadores de transporte público. 
A sua implementação deverá ocorrer entre 2026-2032, sendo o seu financiamento assegurado pela receitas da venda em leilão de emissão do regime CELE.
A sua operacionalização está dependente da finalização da revisão da Diretiva CELE no âmbito do pacote Fit for 55.
A nível nacional, o Fundo Ambiental foi criado através do Decreto-Lei n.º 42-A/2016, de 12 de agosto, para garantir uma maior eficácia da política de ambiente, permitindo, através da extinção de outros fundos, obter um instrumento com maior capacidade financeira e com maior adaptabilidade aos desafios colocados.
column18:
A transição para uma economia de baixo carbono tem muitas vantagens, mas apresenta também uma série de riscos associados. De forma transversal, associada a todo o território, pode dar-se enfâse a vários desafios identificados ao nível da adaptação às alterações climáticas no Plano Municipal de Adaptação às Alterações Climáticas (PMAAC) e, consequentemente, ao nível da mitigação no Plano de Ação para a Energia Sustentável da Maia 2030 (PAES) :
•	A redução da exposição aos riscos climáticos - reduzir a vulnerabilidade climática dos setores estratégicos e dos territórios mais vulneráveis aumentando a capacidade de resposta para lidar com o agravamento dos riscos climáticos;
•	O aumento da capacidade adaptativa - promover o reforço da capacidade adaptativa local, criando condições para que os diversos atores locais lidem com os desafios das alterações climáticas e integrem a adaptação nos seus planos, estratégias e projetos;
•	A promoção da cooperação territorial para a adaptação - reforçar a governação local e intermunicipal integrada (vertical e horizontalmente) aumentando a capacidade de responder de forma coordenada, com eficácia e eficiência, aos desafios das alterações climáticas;
•	O aumento da consciencialização - aumentar a consciencialização das comunidades locais para os impactes e oportunidades das alterações climáticas e para o imperativo da adaptação;
•	A promoção da monitorização - assegurar um acompanhamento regular da evolução climática do concelho, dos impactes das alterações climáticas e da evolução da capacidade adaptativa dos atores, setores e territórios vulneráveis
Para além disto, foram identificados alguns potenciais riscos/constrangimentos à implementação das medidas de adaptação previstas:
•	Dificuldade na sensibilização do público-alvo à mudança de comportamentos 
•	Falta de elementos para a realização de diagnósticos necessários à implementação de determinadas ações 
•	Disponibilidade de recursos humanos e financeiros para a execução das ações
•	Dificuldade na articulação entre os intervenientes das entidades envolvidas
•	Integração dos vários sistemas de monitorização previstos
•	Elevado custo e manutenção de certos equipamentos
•	Elevada pressão urbana · 
•	Dificuldade na identificação dos proprietários de terrenos a necessitarem de intervenção; Dificuldade de acesso.

column15: O município iniciou a sua ação com a definição do Plano de Ação para a Energia Sustentável e Clima (SECAP), passando este a funcionar como \numa ferramenta de suporte à elaboração do plano municipal de adaptação às alterações climáticas (PMAAC) publicado em abr.23 e à elaboração do plano municipal de ação climática (PMAC), aprovado em reunião do Município no início de set.25 para lançamento para consulta pública ainda em set.25.
column16: A identificação de riscos associados às alterações climáticas na região, incluindo as vulnerabilidades existentes e projetadas, tornou-se indispensável na definição do roteiro estratégico que permite ter estes riscos claramente identificados e com um plano de abordagem que minimiza impactos futuros, aumentando a resiliência diante os desafios climáticos.\nO plano de adaptação (PMAAC) permite potenciar a proteção da saúde pública e a preservação da biodiversidade e dos ecossistemas, com o planeamento proativo a longo prazo que reduz a exposição do município às consequência futuras das alterações climáticas, sendo reforçado pelo plano de ação (PMAC).
column17: Com as consequências previstas atuais e projetadas para o futuro, resultantes das alterações climáticas, combinadas com os recursos financeiros limitados disponíveis, o município passou a ter de considerar a identificação atempada de linhas de financiamento que permitam a concretização dos planos (PMAAC e PMAC). De forma a reduzir o nível de dependência entre a execução de ações climáticas e as linhas de financiamento disponíveis, o Município está a iniciar a identificação de outros tipos de fontes de financiamento, tais como: 1) ajuda em espécie, 2) medidas fiscais, 3) venda/arrendamento de ativos locais, 4) inclusão de capital privado, 5) financiamento misto (incluindo parcerias público-privadas) ou 6) Crowdfunding (financiamento coletivo).

O Município da Figueira da Foz aprovou, em 2016, a Estratégia Municipal de Adaptação às Alterações Climáticas (EMAAC), que previa opções de adaptação. Uma vez que o Plano Diretor Municipal se encontrava em fase de revisão, à data, algumas das opções foram transpostas para este instrumento de gestão territorial de modo a coincidirem com o processo em curso. Importa também referir que existiram claras interações determinantes face à relação entre programas de âmbito nacional, regional e municipal, em particular com os seguintes: 
• Programa da Orla Costeira (POC) Ovar - Marinha Grande, nomeadamente no que diz respeito às opções de adaptação
“Alimentação artificial das praias do sul do concelho através do desassoreamento do Rio Mondego no canal portuário da Figueira da Foz” e “Introdução do recuo progressivo da edificação nas zonas costeiras, considerando critérios como a baixa cota altimétrica para justificar e definir áreas non aedificandi”;
• Plano Municipal de Emergência e Proteção Civil, no que diz respeito às opções de adaptação
“Promoção de sessões de formação/educação da população no âmbito de opções/soluções de
adaptação para as alterações climáticas e riscos consequentes” e “Criação de regulação municipal especifica para as zonas de risco potencial de cheias, inundações e erosão costeira”;
• Plano de Ordenamento de Estuário do Mondego (ainda não realizado), no que respeita à
elaboração do Plano de Gestão da Morraceira.
column17: Atualmente, o acesso a ferramentas de apoio a fontes de financiamento (quer da União Europeia, de fundos nacionais, do orçamento municipal, entre outras) para a implementação das medidas e ações preconizadas, é essencial para o sucesso da implementação do PMAC/PAESC, uma vez que o municípo dispõe de verba própria, no entanto, com algumas limitações face às necessidades globais.\nPor outro lado, algumas medidas significativas que serão implementadas no Município, decorrentes das alterações climáticas, não se verificam impactantes ao nível financeiro uma vez que são da responsabilidade da Administração Central. \nA título de exemplo, de referir que um dos problemas mais graves sentidos no Município da Figueira da Foz diz respeito à erosão costeira e à necessidade de se promover a alimentação artificial das praias do sul do concelho, com a construção de um sistema fixo de bypass a norte do molhe norte da Figueira da Foz e respetivas saídas na zona da Cova-Gala, com o objetivo de repor o balanço sedimentar no troço costeiro. Estas intervenções permitirão uma minimização do recuo da linha de costa relativamente à situação atual entre a Cova-Gala e a Leirosa, com minimização dos galgamentos costeiros, dinamização do setor turístico e melhoria na qualidade de vida das populações locais. Importa sobre este aspeto referir que a responsabilidade por esta intervenção é da Agência Portuguesa do Ambiente.
column18:
Reconhecendo o compromisso assumido por Portugal e pelo Município da Figueira da Foz
face à neutralidade carbónica até 2050, assumindo a inevitabilidade da transição energética dada a urgência climática e tendo consciência da necessidade de mudança do paradigma económico, em particular no que respeita aos combustíveis fósseis, face aos níveis atuais de Gases com Efeito de Estufa, pretende-se encontrar mecanismos de mitigação, que conduzam a uma redução das emissões de gases com efeito de estufa, contribuindo desta forma para a redução do aquecimento global do planeta.
Neste contexto, o Município dispõe de um Plano Municipal de Ação Climática (PMAC), o qual inclui medidas de mitigação, nomeadamente no que respeita à Área da Energia, que permitirão concretizar a transição energética, aumentando significativamente a eficiência energética em todos os setores da economia e apostando na incorporação de fontes de energia renováveis endógenas.
O PMAC pretende fomentar o correto planeamento e desenvolvimento de uma
sociedade e economia resiliente, competitiva e de baixo carbono, tal como preconizado na
Estratégia Nacional de Adaptação às Alterações Climáticas 2020 (ENAAC 2020), indo assim ao
encontro dos Objetivos de Desenvolvimento Sustentável e do Pilar Europeu dos Direitos Sociais.
